يَدَيْهِ مِنْهَا فَتَوَضَّأَ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ مَنِ الْمَرْأَتَانِ مِنْ أَزْوَاجِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم اللَّتَانِ قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى ‏[quran sura="66" aya_start="4" aya_end="4"]{‏إِنْ تَتُوبَا إِلَى اللَّهِ فَقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُمَا‏}‏ قَالَ وَاعَجَبًا لَكَ يَا ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ، هُمَا عَائِشَةُ وَحَفْصَةُ‏.‏ ثُمَّ اسْتَقْبَلَ عُمَرُ الْحَدِيثَ يَسُوقُهُ قَالَ كُنْتُ أَنَا وَجَارٌ لِي مِنَ الأَنْصَارِ فِي بَنِي أُمَيَّةَ بْنِ زَيْدٍ، وَهُمْ مِنْ عَوَالِي الْمَدِينَةِ، وَكُنَّا نَتَنَاوَبُ النُّزُولَ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَيَنْزِلُ يَوْمًا وَأَنْزِلُ يَوْمًا، فَإِذَا نَزَلْتُ جِئْتُهُ بِمَا حَدَثَ مِنْ خَبَرِ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ مِنَ الْوَحْىِ أَوْ غَيْرِهِ، وَإِذَا نَزَلَ فَعَلَ مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ، وَكُنَّا مَعْشَرَ قُرَيْشٍ نَغْلِبُ النِّسَاءَ، فَلَمَّا قَدِمْنَا عَلَى الأَنْصَارِ إِذَا قَوْمٌ تَغْلِبُهُمْ نِسَاؤُهُمْ، فَطَفِقَ نِسَاؤُنَا يَأْخُذْنَ مِنْ أَدَبِ نِسَاءِ الأَنْصَارِ، فَصَخِبْتُ عَلَى امْرَأَتِي فَرَاجَعَتْنِي فَأَنْكَرْتُ أَنْ تُرَاجِعَنِي قَالَتْ وَلِمَ تُنْكِرُ أَنْ أُرَاجِعَكَ فَوَاللَّهِ إِنَّ أَزْوَاجَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم لَيُرَاجِعْنَهُ، وَإِنَّ إِحْدَاهُنَّ لَتَهْجُرُهُ الْيَوْمَ حَتَّى اللَّيْلِ‏.‏ فَأَفْزَعَنِي ذَلِكَ وَقُلْتُ لَهَا وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنْ فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ مِنْهُنَّ‏.‏ ثُمَّ جَمَعْتُ عَلَىَّ ثِيَابِي فَنَزَلْتُ فَدَخَلْتُ عَلَى حَفْصَةَ فَقُلْتُ لَهَا أَىْ حَفْصَةُ أَتُغَاضِبُ إِحْدَاكُنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم الْيَوْمَ حَتَّى اللَّيْلِ قَالَتْ نَعَمْ‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ قَدْ خِبْتِ وَخَسِرْتِ، أَفَتَأْمَنِينَ أَنْ يَغْضَبَ اللَّهُ لِغَضَبِ رَسُولِهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَتَهْلِكِي لاَ تَسْتَكْثِرِي النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَلاَ تُرَاجِعِيهِ فِي شَىْءٍ، وَلاَ تَهْجُرِيهِ، وَسَلِينِي مَا بَدَا لَكِ، وَلاَ يَغُرَّنَّكِ أَنْ كَانَتْ جَارَتُكِ أَوْضَأَ مِنْكِ، وَأَحَبَّ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ يُرِيدُ عَائِشَةَ ـ قَالَ عُمَرُ وَكُنَّا قَدْ تَحَدَّثْنَا أَنَّ غَسَّانَ تُنْعِلُ الْخَيْلَ لِغَزْوِنَا، فَنَزَلَ صَاحِبِي الأَنْصَارِيُّ يَوْمَ نَوْبَتِهِ، فَرَجَعَ إِلَيْنَا عِشَاءً فَضَرَبَ بَابِي ضَرْبًا شَدِيدًا وَقَالَ أَثَمَّ هُوَ فَفَزِعْتُ فَخَرَجْتُ إِلَيْهِ، فَقَالَ قَدْ حَدَثَ الْيَوْمَ أَمْرٌ عَظِيمٌ‏.‏ قُلْتُ مَا هُوَ، أَجَاءَ غَسَّانُ قَالَ لاَ بَلْ أَعْظَمُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ وَأَهْوَلُ، طَلَّقَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم نِسَاءَهُ‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ خَابَتْ حَفْصَةُ وَخَسِرَتْ، قَدْ كُنْتُ أَظُنُّ هَذَا يُوشِكُ أَنْ يَكُونَ، فَجَمَعْتُ عَلَىَّ ثِيَابِي فَصَلَّيْتُ صَلاَةَ الْفَجْرِ مَعَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَدَخَلَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم مَشْرُبَةً لَهُ، فَاعْتَزَلَ فِيهَا، وَدَخَلْتُ عَلَى حَفْصَةَ فَإِذَا هِيَ تَبْكِي فَقُلْتُ مَا يُبْكِيكِ أَلَمْ أَكُنْ حَذَّرْتُكِ هَذَا أَطَلَّقَكُنَّ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَتْ لاَ أَدْرِي هَا هُوَ ذَا مُعْتَزِلٌ فِي الْمَشْرُبَةِ‏.‏ فَخَرَجْتُ فَجِئْتُ إِلَى الْمِنْبَرِ فَإِذَا حَوْلَهُ رَهْطٌ يَبْكِي بَعْضُهُمْ، فَجَلَسْتُ مَعَهُمْ قَلِيلاً ثُمَّ غَلَبَنِي مَا أَجِدُ، فَجِئْتُ الْمَشْرُبَةَ الَّتِي فِيهَا النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقُلْتُ لِغُلاَمٍ لَهُ أَسْوَدَ اسْتَأْذِنْ لِعُمَرَ‏.‏ فَدَخَلَ الْغُلاَمُ فَكَلَّمَ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ثُمَّ رَجَعَ فَقَالَ كَلَّمْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَذَكَرْتُكَ لَهُ، فَصَمَتَ‏.‏ فَانْصَرَفْتُ حَتَّى جَلَسْتُ مَعَ الرَّهْطِ الَّذِينَ عِنْدَ الْمِنْبَرِ، ثُمَّ غَلَبَنِي مَا أَجِدُ فَجِئْتُ فَقُلْتُ لِلْغُلاَمِ اسْتَأْذِنْ لِعُمَرَ‏.‏ فَدَخَلَ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ فَقَالَ قَدْ ذَكَرْتُكَ لَهُ فَصَمَتَ‏.‏ فَرَجَعْتُ فَجَلَسْتُ مَعَ الرَّهْطِ الَّذِينَ عِنْدَ الْمِنْبَرِ، ثُمَّ غَلَبَنِي مَا أَجِدُ فَجِئْتُ الْغُلاَمَ فَقُلْتُ اسْتَأْذِنْ لِعُمَرَ‏.‏ فَدَخَلَ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ إِلَىَّ فَقَالَ قَدْ ذَكَرْتُكَ لَهُ فَصَمَتَ‏.‏ فَلَمَّا وَلَّيْتُ مُنْصَرِفًا ـ قَالَ ـ إِذَا الْغُلاَمُ يَدْعُونِي فَقَالَ قَدْ أَذِنَ لَكَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَدَخَلْتُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَإِذَا هُوَ مُضْطَجِعٌ عَلَى رِمَالِ حَصِيرٍ، لَيْسَ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَهُ فِرَاشٌ، قَدْ أَثَّرَ الرِّمَالُ بِجَنْبِهِ مُتَّكِئًا عَلَى وِسَادَةٍ مِنْ أَدَمٍ حَشْوُهَا لِيفٌ، فَسَلَّمْتُ عَلَيْهِ ثُمَّ قُلْتُ وَأَنَا قَائِمٌ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَطَلَّقْتَ نِسَاءَكَ‏.‏ فَرَفَعَ إِلَىَّ بَصَرَهُ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ لاَ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ‏.‏ ثُمَّ قُلْتُ وَأَنَا قَائِمٌ أَسْتَأْنِسُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ لَوْ رَأَيْتَنِي، وَكُنَّا مَعْشَرَ قُرَيْشٍ نَغْلِبُ النِّسَاءَ فَلَمَّا قَدِمْنَا الْمَدِينَةَ إِذَا قَوْمٌ تَغْلِبُهُمْ نِسَاؤُهُمْ، فَتَبَسَّمَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ثُمَّ قُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ لَوْ رَأَيْتَنِي وَدَخَلْتُ عَلَى حَفْصَةَ فَقُلْتُ لَهَا لاَ يَغُرَّنَّكِ أَنْ كَانَتْ جَارَتُكِ أَوْضَأَ مِنْكِ وَأَحَبَّ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يُرِيدُ عَائِشَةَ فَتَبَسَّمَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم تَبَسُّمَةً أُخْرَى، فَجَلَسْتُ حِينَ رَأَيْتُهُ تَبَسَّمَ، فَرَفَعْتُ بَصَرِي فِي بَيْتِهِ، فَوَاللَّهِ مَا رَأَيْتُ فِي بَيْتِهِ شَيْئًا يَرُدُّ الْبَصَرَ غَيْرَ أَهَبَةٍ ثَلاَثَةٍ، فَقُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ادْعُ اللَّهَ فَلْيُوَسِّعْ عَلَى أُمَّتِكَ، فَإِنَّ فَارِسًا وَالرُّومَ قَدْ وُسِّعَ عَلَيْهِمْ، وَأُعْطُوا الدُّنْيَا وَهُمْ لاَ يَعْبُدُونَ اللَّهَ‏.‏ فَجَلَسَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَكَانَ مُتَّكِئًا‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ أَوَفِي هَذَا أَنْتَ يَا ابْنَ الْخَطَّابِ، إِنَّ أُولَئِكَ قَوْمٌ عُجِّلُوا طَيِّبَاتِهِمْ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ اسْتَغْفِرْ لِي‏.‏ فَاعْتَزَلَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم نِسَاءَهُ مِنْ أَجْلِ ذَلِكَ الْحَدِيثِ حِينَ أَفْشَتْهُ حَفْصَةُ إِلَى عَائِشَةَ تِسْعًا وَعِشْرِينَ لَيْلَةً وَكَانَ قَالَ ‏"‏ مَا أَنَا بِدَاخِلٍ عَلَيْهِنَّ شَهْرًا ‏"‏‏.‏ مِنْ شِدَّةِ مَوْجِدَتِهِ عَلَيْهِنَّ حِينَ عَاتَبَهُ اللَّهُ، فَلَمَّا مَضَتْ تِسْعٌ وَعِشْرُونَ لَيْلَةً دَخَلَ عَلَى عَائِشَةَ فَبَدَأَ بِهَا فَقَالَتْ لَهُ عَائِشَةُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنَّكَ كُنْتَ قَدْ أَقْسَمْتَ أَنْ لاَ تَدْخُلَ عَلَيْنَا شَهْرًا، وَإِنَّمَا أَصْبَحْتَ مِنْ تِسْعٍ وَعِشْرِينَ لَيْلَةً أَعُدُّهَا عَدًّا‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ الشَّهْرُ تِسْعٌ وَعِشْرُونَ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَكَانَ ذَلِكَ الشَّهْرُ تِسْعًا وَعِشْرِينَ لَيْلَةً‏.‏ قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ ثُمَّ أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى آيَةَ التَّخَيُّرِ فَبَدَأَ بِي أَوَّلَ امْرَأَةٍ مِنْ نِسَائِهِ فَاخْتَرْتُهُ، ثُمَّ خَيَّرَ نِسَاءَهُ كُلَّهُنَّ فَقُلْنَ مِثْلَ مَا قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ‏.‏
en_text: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Thawr informed me, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: I was always eager to ask ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab about the two wives of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, concerning whom Allah Most High said, ‘If you two repent to Allah, for your hearts have inclined…’ (66:4). I could not ask him until he went for Hajj and I went with him. On the way, he turned aside with a water skin to relieve himself. When he came back, I poured water over his hands from it and he performed ablution. I said to him, ‘Commander of the Faithful, who were the two wives of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, concerning whom Allah Most High said, “If you two repent to Allah, for your hearts have inclined…”’ He said, ‘How astonishing, Ibn ‘Abbas! They were ‘A’ishah and Hafsah.’ Then ‘Umar continued the account: ‘I and a neighbor of mine from the Ansar lived among Banu Umayyah ibn Zayd, in the upper part of Madinah. We used to take turns visiting the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. He would go one day, and I would go the next. When I went, I brought him news of what had happened that day, whether revelation or something else; when my neighbor went, he did the same. We, the Quraysh, used to prevail over our women. When we came among the Ansar, we found a people whose women prevailed over them. Our women began adopting the ways of the Ansari women. I spoke harshly to my wife, but she answered me back, and I objected to her answering me. She said, “Why do you object to my answering you? By Allah, the wives of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, answer him back, and one of them may shun him from morning until night.” That alarmed me, and I said to her, “The one among them who does that has surely failed.” Then I gathered my clothes and went down to Hafsah. I said to her, “Hafsah, does one of you really make the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, angry from morning until night?” She said, “Yes.” I said, “You have failed and lost. Do you feel safe from Allah becoming angry because His Messenger is angry with you, and thereby being ruined? Do not demand too much from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, do not answer him back about anything, and do not shun him. Ask me whatever you wish. Do not be deceived because your co-wife is more beautiful than you and more beloved to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him”—meaning ‘A’ishah. ‘Umar said: We had been talking about how Ghassan was preparing horses for our expedition. On my neighbor’s appointed day, he went to visit the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and returned to us in the evening. He pounded hard on my door and said, “Is he there?” I was alarmed and went out to him. He said, “Something tremendous happened today.” I asked, “What is it? Has Ghassan come?” He said, “No, something greater and more alarming: the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, has divorced his wives.” I said, “Hafsah has failed and lost! I thought this was about to happen.” I gathered my clothes and prayed the dawn prayer with the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. He entered an upper room of his and secluded himself there. I went to Hafsah and found her weeping. I said, “What makes you weep? Had I not warned you about this? Has the Prophet divorced you?” She said, “I do not know. Here he is, secluded in the upper room.” I went out and came to the pulpit, where I found a group of people around it, some of them weeping. I sat with them for a little while, but what I was feeling overcame me. I went to the upper room where the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was and said to a black servant of his, “Ask permission for ‘Umar.” The servant went in, spoke to the Prophet, and returned. He said, “I mentioned you to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and he was silent.” I went back and sat with the group by the pulpit. Then what I was feeling overcame me again, so I went and said to the servant, “Ask permission for ‘Umar.” He went in and returned, saying, “I mentioned you to him, and he was silent.” I went back and sat with the group by the pulpit. Then what I was feeling overcame me again, so I went to the servant and said, “Ask permission for ‘Umar.” He went in and returned to me, saying, “He was silent when I mentioned you.” As I turned to leave, the servant called me and said, “The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, has given you permission.” I entered to see the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and found him lying on a mat of woven palm leaves, with no bedding between him and it; the mat had left marks on his side. He was leaning on a leather pillow stuffed with palm fiber. I greeted him and, while standing, said, “Messenger of Allah, have you divorced your wives?” He looked up at me and said, “No.” I said, “Allah is greatest!” Then, still standing to put him at ease, I said, “Messenger of Allah, if only you had seen me! We Quraysh used to prevail over our women, but when we came to Madinah we found a people whose women prevail over them.” The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, smiled. Then I said, “Messenger of Allah, if only you had seen me when I went to Hafsah and said, ‘Do not be deceived because your co-wife is more beautiful than you and more beloved to the Prophet’”—meaning ‘A’ishah. The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, smiled again. When I saw him smile, I sat down. I looked around his home and, by Allah, I saw nothing that caught the eye except three hides. I said, “Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah to grant your community abundance. The Persians and Romans have been given abundance and worldly goods, although they do not worship Allah.” The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, sat up; he had been reclining. He said, “Is that what concerns you, Ibn al-Khattab? Those people have been given their good things sooner in the life of this world.” I said, “Messenger of Allah, ask Allah to forgive me.” The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, stayed apart from his wives for 29 nights because of that matter, after Hafsah had disclosed it to ‘A’ishah. He had said, “I will not go in to them for a month,” because he was so angry with them after Allah had reproached him. When 29 nights had passed, he went in to ‘A’ishah first. ‘A’ishah said to him, “Messenger of Allah, you swore that you would not come in to us for a month, but I have counted only 29 nights since you began.” He said, “A month is 29 days.” That month was indeed 29 nights. ‘A’ishah said: Then Allah Most High revealed the verse giving the Prophet’s wives a choice. He began with me, the first of his wives, and I chose him. Then he gave all his wives the choice, and they each said what ‘A’ishah had said.

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 5192, book 67, باب صَوْمِ الْمَرْأَةِ بِإِذْنِ زَوْجِهَا تَطَوُّعًا
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُقَاتِلٍ، أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ، أَخْبَرَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنْ هَمَّامِ بْنِ مُنَبِّهٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ لاَ تَصُومُ الْمَرْأَةُ وَبَعْلُهَا شَاهِدٌ إِلاَّ بِإِذْنِهِ ‏"‏‏.‏
en_text: Muhammad ibn Muqatil narrated to us: ‘Abd Allah informed us: Ma‘mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said, ‘A woman should not fast while her husband is present without his permission.’

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 5193, book 67, باب إِذَا بَاتَتِ الْمَرْأَةُ مُهَاجِرَةً فِرَاشَ زَوْجِهَا
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ بَشَّارٍ، حَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ أَبِي عَدِيٍّ، عَنْ شُعْبَةَ، عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ، عَنْ أَبِي حَازِمٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ إِذَا دَعَا الرَّجُلُ امْرَأَتَهُ إِلَى فِرَاشِهِ فَأَبَتْ أَنْ تَجِيءَ لَعَنَتْهَا الْمَلاَئِكَةُ حَتَّى تُصْبِحَ ‏"‏‏.‏
en_text: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Ibn Abi ‘Adi narrated to us, from Shu‘bah, from Sulayman, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said, ‘When a man calls his wife to his bed and she refuses to come, the angels curse her until morning.’

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 5194, book 67, باب إِذَا بَاتَتِ الْمَرْأَةُ مُهَاجِرَةً فِرَاشَ زَوْجِهَا
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَرْعَرَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، عَنْ زُرَارَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ إِذَا بَاتَتِ الْمَرْأَةُ مُهَاجِرَةً فِرَاشَ زَوْجِهَا لَعَنَتْهَا الْمَلاَئِكَةُ حَتَّى تَرْجِعَ ‏"‏‏.‏
en_text: Muhammad ibn ‘Ar‘arah narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Zurarah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘When a woman spends the night abandoning her husband’s bed, the angels curse her until she returns.’

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 5195, book 67, باب لاَ تَأْذَنُ الْمَرْأَةُ فِي بَيْتِ زَوْجِهَا لأَحَدٍ إِلاَّ بِإِذْنِهِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو الْيَمَانِ، أَخْبَرَنَا شُعَيْبٌ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو الزِّنَادِ، عَنِ الأَعْرَجِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، رضى الله عنه أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ لاَ يَحِلُّ لِلْمَرْأَةِ أَنْ تَصُومَ وَزَوْجُهَا شَاهِدٌ إِلاَّ بِإِذْنِهِ، وَلاَ تَأْذَنَ فِي بَيْتِهِ إِلاَّ بِإِذْنِهِ، وَمَا أَنْفَقَتْ مِنْ نَفَقَةٍ عَنْ غَيْرِ أَمْرِهِ فَإِنَّهُ يُؤَدَّى إِلَيْهِ شَطْرُهُ ‏"‏‏.‏ وَرَوَاهُ أَبُو الزِّنَادِ أَيْضًا عَنْ مُوسَى عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ فِي الصَّوْمِ‏.‏
en_text: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us: Shu‘ayb informed us: Abu al-Zinad narrated to us, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘It is not lawful for a woman to fast while her husband is present without his permission, or to admit anyone into his house without his permission. Whatever she spends from his property without his instruction, half of it is returned to him.’ Abu al-Zinad also narrated it, from Musa, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, concerning the fast.

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 5196, book 67, كتاب النكاح
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مُسَدَّدٌ، حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ، أَخْبَرَنَا التَّيْمِيُّ، عَنْ أَبِي عُثْمَانَ، عَنْ أُسَامَةَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ قُمْتُ عَلَى باب الْجَنَّةِ فَكَانَ عَامَّةَ مَنْ دَخَلَهَا الْمَسَاكِينُ، وَأَصْحَابُ الْجَدِّ مَحْبُوسُونَ، غَيْرَ أَنَّ أَصْحَابَ النَّارِ قَدْ أُمِرَ بِهِمْ إِلَى النَّارِ، وَقُمْتُ عَلَى باب النَّارِ فَإِذَا عَامَّةُ مَنْ دَخَلَهَا النِّسَاءُ ‏"‏‏.‏
en_text: Musaddad narrated to us: Isma‘il narrated to us: Al-Taymi informed us, from Abu ‘Uthman, from Usamah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said, ‘I stood at the gate of Paradise, and most of those who entered it were the poor, while the wealthy were held back. The people of the Fire had already been ordered to the Fire. Then I stood at the gate of the Fire, and most of those who entered it were women.’

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 5197, book 67, باب كُفْرَانِ الْعَشِيرِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ يُوسُفَ، أَخْبَرَنَا مَالِكٌ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، عَنْ عَطَاءِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ خَسَفَتِ الشَّمْسُ عَلَى عَهْدِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَصَلَّى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَالنَّاسُ مَعَهُ، فَقَامَ قِيَامًا طَوِيلاً نَحْوًا مِنْ سُورَةِ الْبَقَرَةِ، ثُمَّ رَكَعَ رُكُوعًا طَوِيلاً، ثُمَّ رَفَعَ فَقَامَ قِيَامًا طَوِيلاً وَهْوَ دُونَ الْقِيَامِ الأَوَّلِ، ثُمَّ رَكَعَ رُكُوعًا طَوِيلاً وَهْوَ دُونَ الرُّكُوعِ الأَوَّلِ، ثُمَّ سَجَدَ، ثُمَّ قَامَ فَقَامَ قِيَامًا طَوِيلاً وَهْوَ دُونَ الْقِيَامِ الأَوَّلِ، ثُمَّ رَكَعَ رُكُوعًا طَوِيلاً وَهْوَ دُونَ الرُّكُوعِ الأَوَّلِ، ثُمَّ رَفَعَ فَقَامَ قِيَامًا طَوِيلاً وَهْوَ دُونَ الْقِيَامِ الأَوَّلِ، ثُمَّ رَكَعَ رُكُوعًا طَوِيلاً وَهْوَ دُونَ الرُّكُوعِ الأَوَّلِ، ثُمَّ رَفَعَ ثُمَّ سَجَدَ، ثُمَّ انْصَرَفَ، وَقَدْ تَجَلَّتِ الشَّمْسُ، فَقَالَ ‏"‏ إِنَّ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ آيَتَانِ مِنْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ لاَ يَخْسِفَانِ لِمَوْتِ أَحَدٍ وَلاَ لِحَيَاتِهِ، فَإِذَا رَأَيْتُمْ ذَلِكَ فَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالُوا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ رَأَيْنَاكَ تَنَاوَلْتَ شَيْئًا فِي مَقَامِكَ هَذَا، ثُمَّ رَأَيْنَاكَ تَكَعْكَعْتَ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ الْجَنَّةَ ـ أَوْ أُرِيتُ الْجَنَّةَ ـ فَتَنَاوَلْتُ مِنْهَا عُنْقُودًا وَلَوْ أَخَذْتُهُ لأَكَلْتُمْ مِنْهُ مَا بَقِيَتِ الدُّنْيَا، وَرَأَيْتُ النَّارَ فَلَمْ أَرَ كَالْيَوْمِ مَنْظَرًا قَطُّ وَرَأَيْتُ أَكْثَرَ أَهْلِهَا النِّسَاءَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالُوا لِمَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ قَالَ ‏"‏ بِكُفْرِهِنَّ ‏"‏‏.‏ قِيلَ يَكْفُرْنَ بِاللَّهِ قَالَ ‏"‏ يَكْفُرْنَ الْعَشِيرَ، وَيَكْفُرْنَ الإِحْسَانَ، وَلَوْ أَحْسَنْتَ إِلَى إِحْدَاهُنَّ الدَّهْرَ، ثُمَّ رَأَتْ مِنْكَ شَيْئًا قَالَتْ مَا رَأَيْتُ مِنْكَ خَيْرًا قَطُّ ‏"‏‏.‏
en_text: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us: Malik informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abbas, who said: The sun was eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. The Messenger of Allah prayed, and the people prayed with him. He stood for a long time, about as long as it takes to recite Surah al-Baqarah. Then he bowed for a long time, rose and stood for a long time, but less than the first standing, then bowed for a long time, but less than the first bowing, and then prostrated. Then he stood and stood for a long time, less than the first standing, then bowed for a long time, less than the first bowing, then rose and stood for a long time, less than the first standing, then bowed for a long time, less than the first bowing, then rose and prostrated. He then finished, and the sun had become clear. He said, ‘The sun and the moon are two of Allah’s signs; they do not eclipse because of anyone’s death or life. When you see that, remember Allah.’ They said, ‘Messenger of Allah, we saw you reach for something from where you stood, then we saw you draw back.’ He said, ‘I saw—or was shown—Paradise, and I reached for a cluster of its fruit. Had I taken it, you would have eaten from it for as long as the world remained. I also saw the Fire, and I have never seen a sight like it today. I saw that most of its people were women.’ They asked, ‘Why, Messenger of Allah?’ He said, ‘Because of their ingratitude.’ It was asked, ‘Do they disbelieve in Allah?’ He said, ‘They are ungrateful to their husbands and ungrateful for kindness. If you were kind to one of them throughout a lifetime, then she saw one thing from you, she would say, “I have never seen any good from you.”’

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 5198, book 67, باب كُفْرَانِ الْعَشِيرِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عُثْمَانُ بْنُ الْهَيْثَمِ، حَدَّثَنَا عَوْفٌ، عَنْ أَبِي رَجَاءٍ، عَنْ عِمْرَانَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ اطَّلَعْتُ فِي الْجَنَّةِ فَرَأَيْتُ أَكْثَرَ أَهْلِهَا الْفُقَرَاءَ، وَاطَّلَعْتُ فِي النَّارِ، فَرَأَيْتُ أَكْثَرَ أَهْلِهَا النِّسَاءَ ‏"‏‏.‏ تَابَعَهُ أَيُّوبُ وَسَلْمُ بْنُ زَرِيرٍ‏.‏
en_text: ‘Uthman ibn al-Haytham narrated to us: ‘Awf narrated to us, from Abu Raja’, from ‘Imran, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said, ‘I looked into Paradise and saw that most of its people were the poor. I looked into the Fire and saw that most of its people were women.’ Ayyub and Sallam ibn Zarir also related it.

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 5199, book 67, باب لِزَوْجِكَ عَلَيْكَ حَقٌّ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُقَاتِلٍ، أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ، أَخْبَرَنَا الأَوْزَاعِيُّ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ أَبِي كَثِيرٍ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي أَبُو سَلَمَةَ بْنُ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَاصِ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ يَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ أَلَمْ أُخْبَرْ أَنَّكَ تَصُومُ النَّهَارَ وَتَقُومُ اللَّيْلَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قُلْتُ بَلَى يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ فَلاَ تَفْعَلْ، صُمْ وَأَفْطِرْ، وَقُمْ وَنَمْ، فَإِنَّ لِجَسَدِكَ عَلَيْكَ حَقًّا، وَإِنَّ لِعَيْنِكَ عَلَيْكَ حَقًّا، وَإِنَّ لِزَوْجِكَ عَلَيْكَ حَقًّا ‏"‏‏.‏
en_text: Muhammad ibn Muqatil narrated to us: ‘Abd Allah informed us: Al-Awza‘i informed us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to me: Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman narrated to me: ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amr ibn al-‘As narrated to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘‘Abd Allah, have I not been told that you fast during the day and pray at night?’ I said, ‘Yes, Messenger of Allah.’ He said, ‘Do not do that. Fast and break your fast; pray and sleep. Your body has a right over you, your eyes have a right over you, and your wife has a right over you.’’

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 5200, book 67, باب الْمَرْأَةُ رَاعِيَةٌ فِي بَيْتِ زَوْجِهَا
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدَانُ، أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ، أَخْبَرَنَا مُوسَى بْنُ عُقْبَةَ، عَنْ نَافِعٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ كُلُّكُمْ رَاعٍ، وَكُلُّكُمْ مَسْئُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ، وَالأَمِيرُ رَاعٍ، وَالرَّجُلُ رَاعٍ عَلَى أَهْلِ بَيْتِهِ، وَالْمَرْأَةُ رَاعِيَةٌ عَلَى بَيْتِ زَوْجِهَا وَوَلَدِهِ، فَكُلُّكُمْ رَاعٍ وَكُلُّكُمْ مَسْئُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ ‏"‏‏.‏
en_text: ‘Abdan narrated to us: ‘Abd Allah informed us: Musa ibn ‘Uqbah informed us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said, ‘Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock. The ruler is a shepherd; a man is a shepherd over his household; and a woman is a shepherd over her husband’s house and his children. Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock.’

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 5201, book 67, بَابُ قَوْلِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى: {الرِّجَالُ قَوَّامُونَ عَلَى النِّسَاءِ بِمَا فَضَّلَ اللَّهُ بَعْضَهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ} إِلَى قَوْلِهِ: {إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيًّا كَبِيرًا}
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا خَالِدُ بْنُ مَخْلَدٍ، حَدَّثَنَا سُلَيْمَانُ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي حُمَيْدٌ، عَنْ أَنَسٍ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ قَالَ آلَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِنْ نِسَائِهِ شَهْرًا وَقَعَدَ فِي مَشْرُبَةٍ لَهُ فَنَزَلَ لِتِسْعٍ وَعِشْرِينَ فَقِيلَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنَّكَ آلَيْتَ عَلَى شَهْرٍ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ إِنَّ الشَّهْرَ تِسْعٌ وَعِشْرُونَ ‏"‏‏.‏
en_text: Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us: Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Humayd narrated to me, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, swore to stay away from his wives for a month and remained in an upper room of his. He came down after 29 days. It was said to him, ‘Messenger of Allah, you swore to stay away for a month.’ He said, ‘A month is 29 days.’

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 5202, book 67, باب هِجْرَةِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم نِسَاءَهُ فِي غَيْرِ بُيُوتِهِنَّ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو عَاصِمٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ،‏.‏ وَحَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُقَاتِلٍ، أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ، أَخْبَرَنَا ابْنُ جُرَيْجٍ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ صَيْفِيٍّ، أَنَّ عِكْرِمَةَ بْنَ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ الْحَارِثِ، أَخْبَرَهُ أَنَّ أُمَّ سَلَمَةَ أَخْبَرَتْهُ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم حَلَفَ لاَ يَدْخُلُ عَلَى بَعْضِ أَهْلِهِ شَهْرًا، فَلَمَّا مَضَى تِسْعَةٌ وَعِشْرُونَ يَوْمًا غَدَا عَلَيْهِنَّ أَوْ رَاحَ فَقِيلَ لَهُ يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ حَلَفْتَ أَنْ لاَ تَدْخُلَ عَلَيْهِنَّ شَهْرًا قَالَ ‏"‏ إِنَّ الشَّهْرَ يَكُونُ تِسْعَةً وَعِشْرِينَ يَوْمًا ‏"‏‏.‏
en_text: Abu ‘Asim narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj. Muhammad ibn Muqatil narrated to me: ‘Abd Allah informed us: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: Yahya ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Sayfi informed me that ‘Ikrimah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith told him that Umm Salamah informed him that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, swore that he would not visit some of his wives for a month. When 29 days had passed, he went to them in the morning or evening. It was said to him, ‘Prophet of Allah, you swore not to visit them for a month.’ He said, ‘A month can be 29 days.’

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 5203, book 67, باب هِجْرَةِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم نِسَاءَهُ فِي غَيْرِ بُيُوتِهِنَّ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، حَدَّثَنَا مَرْوَانُ بْنُ مُعَاوِيَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو يَعْفُورٍ، قَالَ تَذَاكَرْنَا عِنْدَ أَبِي الضُّحَى فَقَالَ حَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ، قَالَ أَصْبَحْنَا يَوْمًا وَنِسَاءُ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَبْكِينَ، عِنْدَ كُلِّ امْرَأَةٍ مِنْهُنَّ أَهْلُهَا، فَخَرَجْتُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ، فَإِذَا هُوَ مَلآنُ مِنَ النَّاسِ فَجَاءَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ فَصَعِدَ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهْوَ فِي غُرْفَةٍ لَهُ، فَسَلَّمَ فَلَمْ يُجِبْهُ أَحَدٌ، ثُمَّ سَلَّمَ فَلَمْ يُجِبْهُ أَحَدٌ، ثُمَّ سَلَّمَ فَلَمْ يُجِبْهُ أَحَدٌ، فَنَادَاهُ فَدَخَلَ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ أَطَلَّقْتَ نِسَاءَكَ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ لاَ وَلَكِنْ آلَيْتُ مِنْهُنَّ شَهْرًا ‏"‏‏.‏ فَمَكَثَ تِسْعًا وَعِشْرِينَ، ثُمَّ دَخَلَ عَلَى نِسَائِهِ‏.‏
en_text: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to us: Marwan ibn Mu‘awiyah narrated to us: Abu Ya‘fur narrated to us, saying: While we were discussing this with Abu al-Duha, he said: Ibn ‘Abbas narrated to us: One morning, the wives of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, were weeping, with their families beside each of them. I went out to the mosque and found it full of people. ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab came and went up to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who was in an upper room of his. ‘Umar greeted him, but no one answered. He greeted him a second time, but no one answered. He greeted him a third time, but no one answered. Then he called out, entered to see the Prophet, and asked, ‘Have you divorced your wives?’ He said, ‘No, but I have sworn to stay away from them for a month.’ He remained apart for 29 days, then went in to his wives.

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 5204, book 67, باب مَا يُكْرَهُ مِنْ ضَرْبِ النِّسَاءِ وَقَوْلِهِ ‏{‏وَاضْرِبُوهُنَّ‏}‏ ضَرْبًا غَيْرَ مُبَرِّحٍ‏.‏
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يُوسُفَ، حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ هِشَامٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ زَمْعَةَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ لاَ يَجْلِدُ أَحَدُكُمُ امْرَأَتَهُ جَلْدَ الْعَبْدِ، ثُمَّ يُجَامِعُهَا فِي آخِرِ الْيَوْمِ ‏"‏‏.‏
en_text: Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Zam‘ah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said, ‘None of you should flog his wife as he would flog a slave, then have intercourse with her at the end of the day.’

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 5205, book 67, باب لاَ تُطِيعُ الْمَرْأَةُ زَوْجَهَا فِي مَعْصِيَةٍ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا خَلاَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى، حَدَّثَنَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ نَافِعٍ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ ـ هُوَ ابْنُ مُسْلِمٍ ـ عَنْ صَفِيَّةَ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، أَنَّ امْرَأَةً، مِنَ الأَنْصَارِ زَوَّجَتِ ابْنَتَهَا فَتَمَعَّطَ شَعَرُ رَأْسِهَا، فَجَاءَتْ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَذَكَرَتْ ذَلِكَ لَهُ، فَقَالَتْ إِنَّ زَوْجَهَا أَمَرَنِي أَنْ أَصِلَ فِي شَعَرِهَا‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ لاَ إِنَّهُ قَدْ لُعِنَ الْمُوصِلاَتُ ‏"‏‏.‏
en_text: Khallad ibn Yahya narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Nafi‘ narrated to us, from al-Hasan—namely, Ibn Muslim—from Safiyyah, from ‘A’ishah, that an Ansari woman married off her daughter, whose hair then fell out. She came to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and mentioned this to him. She said, ‘Her husband has told me to add hair to hers.’ He said, ‘No. The women who add hair have been cursed.’

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 5206, book 67, باب ‏ {‏وَإِنِ امْرَأَةٌ خَافَتْ مِنْ بَعْلِهَا نُشُوزًا أَوْ إِعْرَاضًا}
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ ابْنُ سَلاَمٍ، أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو مُعَاوِيَةَ، عَنْ هِشَامٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ ـ رضى الله عنها ـ ‏[quran sura="4" aya_start="128" aya_end="128"]{‏وَإِنِ امْرَأَةٌ خَافَتْ مِنْ بَعْلِهَا نُشُوزًا أَوْ إِعْرَاضًا‏}‏ قَالَتْ هِيَ الْمَرْأَةُ تَكُونُ عِنْدَ الرَّجُلِ، لاَ يَسْتَكْثِرُ مِنْهَا فَيُرِيدُ طَلاَقَهَا، وَيَتَزَوَّجُ غَيْرَهَا، تَقُولُ لَهُ أَمْسِكْنِي وَلاَ تُطَلِّقْنِي، ثُمَّ تَزَوَّجْ غَيْرِي، فَأَنْتَ فِي حِلٍّ مِنَ النَّفَقَةِ عَلَيَّ وَالْقِسْمَةِ لِي، فَذَلِكَ قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى [quran sura="4" aya_start="128" aya_end="128"]‏{‏فَلاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا أَنْ يَصَّالَحَا بَيْنَهُمَا صُلْحًا وَالصُّلْحُ خَيْرٌ‏}‏
en_text: Muhammad ibn Salam narrated to us: Abu Mu‘awiyah informed us, from Hisham, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, concerning the verse, ‘If a woman fears ill treatment or neglect from her husband…’ (4:128). She said: This refers to a woman who is with a man who no longer desires her and wants to divorce her and marry another woman. She says to him, ‘Keep me and do not divorce me; then marry someone else. You are free of any obligation to spend on me or to allot me a turn.’ That is what Allah Most High means when He says, ‘There is no blame upon them if they make a settlement between themselves, and settlement is best’ (4:128).

reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, hadith 5207, book 67, باب الْعَزْلِ
text_original: حَدَّثَنَا مُسَدَّدٌ، حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ سَعِيدٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ، عَنْ عَطَاءٍ، عَنْ جَابِرٍ، قَالَ كُنَّا نَعْزِلُ عَلَى عَهْدِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏
en_text: Musaddad narrated to us: Yahya ibn Sa‘id narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from ‘Ata’, from Jabir, who said: We practiced coitus interruptus during the time of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.
